requirements.requirement: The system shall support four account roles: Dean, Associate Dean, Instructor, Student.
Each account shall belong to exactly one role at a time; role is fixed at provisioning, not user-switchable in production.
The login screen shall authenticate by institutional email and password, no self-registration.
The system shall restrict every route and every navigation item to the roles permitted to see it, server-side and client-side.
A demo-only role switcher may remain in the prototype build, clearly labeled as a demo affordance and excluded from the production build.
Instructor accounts shall be scoped to the subject loads assigned to them for the current semester.
Dean accounts shall have read access to all instructors' syllabi and courseware within the CIT, and approval authority over syllabus/courseware submissions.
Student accounts shall have read access only to courseware published to their enrolled block section.
Session sign-out shall be reachable from the profile menu in the top bar on every screen.
Associate Dean accounts shall be able to import EduSuite-exported records and assign subject loads and block sections, but shall not have syllabus/courseware approval authority.
Associate Dean accounts shall not have access to student performance or score data — that scope belongs to the Instructor and Dean roles.
The Dean's landing dashboard and the Associate Dean's landing dashboard shall be distinct, each reflecting that role's actual responsibilities rather than a shared generic view.
The Instructor shall be able to upload an existing syllabus file, which the system parses into the official KCP format.
After parsing an upload, the system shall present the confirmation prompt "Are you okay with the uploaded syllabus?" before proceeding.
If the instructor declines the parsed result, the system shall ask "What do you want to do next?" and offer re-upload or AI-guided building.
The system shall support AI-guided syllabus building as an alternative to upload, drawing on the CHED-approved curriculum and any files the instructor provides.
The syllabus builder shall capture, per topic: intended learning outcomes, subtopics, timeframes, and planned lessons/activities/assessments, matching the official KCP format.
The syllabus builder shall reference the CHED-approved curriculum inline while the instructor edits, without requiring a separate lookup screen.
The system shall version every syllabus edit and allow the instructor to view prior versions.
The instructor shall be able to download the checked syllabus for offline Dean review, CAO approval and EVP noting, then upload the approved signed file.

The Dean shall review the downloaded syllabus offline and request corrections through that process. EduPulse records the instructor's approved-file attestation and reviewed outline; it does not issue electronic approvals or validate signatures.
The system shall allow syllabus edits mid-semester and shall flag which published courseware items are now out of alignment.
The system shall list all syllabi owned by the logged-in instructor, with status (draft / submitted / approved / needs revision).
The system shall not require the instructor to configure a template before starting — it shall ask and proceed.
The system can be used before subject loads are finalized: syllabus building may start with no uploaded file.
The system shall let the instructor start syllabus work as soon as the EduSuite student list is uploaded, even before block-section assignment is complete.
Each syllabus topic shall link to the CHED curriculum code(s) it maps to.
The syllabus screen shall show, per topic, whether courseware has been generated for it yet.
The system shall support exporting an approved syllabus to a document format for institutional filing.
The system shall not expose model selection, prompt templates, or retrieval configuration on the syllabus screen.

When the instructor selects a course in Section 1, the system shall auto-fill Section 1 (Course, Course Title, Period Offered, Academic Year) and Section 2 (Course Description, Credit Units, Classification, No. of Hours, Prerequisites) from the CHED curriculum reference.
Section 1 (Course Information) and Section 2 (Course Description + metadata) shall be locked (read-only) after course selection — the instructor shall not be able to edit curriculum-sourced fields.
Section 4 (Program Outcomes) shall be prefilled from the curriculum reference but remain editable — the instructor may add, edit, or remove program outcome rows.
No. of Hours shall be calculated as Credit Units × 18 (standard semester formula) and displayed as read-only in Section 2.
The system shall accept a single, unified import of curriculum, subject-load, and student-roster files exported from EduSuite, primarily performed by the Associate Dean.
The system shall not implement live, system-to-system synchronization with EduSuite.
The import screen shall show a log of prior imports with timestamp, file, and row counts accepted/rejected.
The system shall let the Associate Dean or Dean assign imported students to block sections.
The system shall let the Associate Dean or Dean manage block sections and their instructor assignments.

The CHED curriculum reference shall be used as grounding/reference data where relevant (subject pickers when building a syllabus, generation grounding) — not surfaced as its own browsable page or dashboard.
The curriculum reference shall remain read-only in the app; it changes only when CHED replaces it.
The system shall support import even when no syllabus file yet exists, so setup does not block on syllabus readiness.
Import templates (expected column layout) shall be downloadable from the import screen.
The system shall reject and clearly report malformed import rows rather than silently dropping them.

The system shall not present CHED curriculum-mapping coverage as a tracked/exportable metric — no role's job is to monitor curriculum-mapping compliance as a distinct entity; only syllabus-to-courseware alignment (instructor-facing) and section/roster management are monitored.
The system shall generate courseware mapped to an approved syllabus via retrieval-augmented generation grounded in the syllabus and instructor-approved materials.
Generation shall be selectable by whole syllabus, by topic, or by content type (teaching materials, activities, assessments).
Every generated item shall carry a visible, one-line grounding citation (which syllabus topic / curriculum reference it drew from).
The instructor shall review each generated item before it can be published; no AI-generated courseware reaches students unreviewed.
The instructor shall be able to edit a generated item's content and metadata before publishing.
The instructor shall be able to publish an item immediately or schedule it against the syllabus timeframe.
The courseware list shall show status per item: generating / needs review / published / scheduled.
The system shall re-flag published items as out of alignment when the source syllabus topic changes.
The item editor shall support basic metadata (title, topic link, content type) and accessibility fields (alt text, reading level flag).
The item editor shall not expose citation-formatting, localization, or multi-stage editorial-approval tooling beyond what one instructor needs to finish a draft.
The courseware screen shall include an item bank view of previously generated/approved items, filterable by topic.
Generation shall show a live, plain-language progress state ("Retrieving syllabus context… Drafting… Checking alignment…") rather than exposing job-queue internals.
The system shall let the instructor regenerate a single item without regenerating the whole batch.
The system shall log which model/provider generated an item internally, without surfacing model-selection controls to the instructor.
The Dean shall have read access to all published courseware across the college.
The system shall support the three content types named in scope: teaching materials, activities, assessments. No content type outside this list shall be added without a scope update to Ch. 1-2.
Publishing an item shall notify enrolled students of that block section.
The courseware screen shall not include AI-integrity scoring, plagiarism detection, or authorship-verification features.
The system shall allow export of a published courseware item to a common document/presentation/quiz file format.
Consistency checking (generated content vs. syllabus) shall run automatically on generation and on syllabus edit — never as a manually triggered "QA suite."
Students shall be able to take a published assessment (quiz/exam) within the platform.
The system shall auto-score objective item types and let the instructor grade open-response items.
Instructors shall be able to view and adjust a student's recorded score before it counts toward performance data.
The assessment screen shall show, per assessment, which syllabus topic it maps to.
Students shall see their own score and, where enabled, correct-answer review, immediately or on instructor-set release.
The system shall support timed assessments with an instructor-set duration.
The gradebook shall aggregate scores per student, per assessment, without a separate export/report destination.
The system shall not implement integration with the official KCP grading sheet or institutional term-grade computation.
The assessment editor shall reuse the courseware item bank rather than maintaining a separate question repository.
The system shall record assessment attempts with timestamp, for the instructor's own review only (not a compliance/audit surface).
The system shall not implement AI-based plagiarism detection or lockdown/proctoring features.
Students shall be able to submit an appeal on a scored assessment to their instructor.
The system shall support the assessment types named in scope (quizzes/exams as generated activity content); no separate "assessment security" console shall be added.
The system shall visualize student performance against the syllabus, per topic, showing mastered vs. needs-review status.
Students shall see their own performance view: which topics they've mastered, which need review.
Instructors shall see a class-level performance view across their own sections.
The Dean shall see a college-wide performance view, rolled up by instructor and by subject.
The Dean's view shall indicate whether each instructor's syllabus is being satisfied in its delivery.
Score-based threshold alerts (e.g., students below a mastery cutoff) shall surface inside the Performance screen, not a separate alerting console.
The system shall not implement AI-based at-risk prediction beyond score-based monitoring.
Performance data shall be computed from recorded assessment scores; no separate manual-consolidation step shall be required of the instructor.
The performance view shall support export to a shareable report (PDF/CSV) as an action on the screen itself, not a separate "Reports" destination.
Performance charts shall be filterable by section, subject, and date range.
The system shall recompute topic mastery automatically when new scores are recorded — no manual refresh/recalculation step.
The Dean's compliance view shall flag syllabi with no recent courseware activity as a simple status, not a scored "compliance audit."
Student performance data shall be visible only to that student, their instructor(s), and the Dean.
The system shall show historical trend (not just current snapshot) for a student's topic mastery.
Performance visualizations shall use plain mastery/needs-review language, not raw model-confidence or telemetry terms.
The system shall not require a separate "KPI tracker" or project-success-metrics screen inside the product; those are researcher artifacts, not a system feature.
The Dean shall have a single Review Inbox listing syllabi and courseware pending approval.
The Dean shall be able to approve or request changes on a pending syllabus, with a comment.
The Review Inbox shall separate items by status: pending, approved, needs revision.
The Dean shall see a recent-activity feed (approvals, submissions, publications) on their dashboard, in place of a full audit-log console.
Requesting changes shall notify the instructor with the Dean's comment attached.
The Dean shall be able to drill from the Review Inbox into the specific syllabus or courseware item under review.
The system shall not implement a general-purpose policy-exception or approval-chain governance board beyond the syllabus/courseware review flow described in Fig. 2.
The Dean's oversight scope shall be the CIT only; multi-department oversight is out of scope.
The Review Inbox shall show, per instructor, how many topics have generated-but-unpublished courseware.
Dean-level reporting shall be reachable as an export action from Review Inbox / Performance, not a standalone "Reports" section.
The system shall provide a persistent, docked AI guide ("Pulse") rather than a configuration panel, consistent with the assistive/prompt-guided model.
Pulse shall offer contextual help on the field, card, or chart currently focused or dwelt-on by the user.
Contextual help shall be invoked by a left-click on a dwell-triggered badge, or by a keyboard shortcut when the element has focus — never by hijacking the browser's native right-click menu.
Pulse shall be reachable via keyboard alone, for users who do not use a mouse.
Pulse shall render as a 2D animated character (SVG/vector-animation based), not a real-time 3D rig.
Pulse shall support at minimum these expression states: idle, curious, thinking, encouraging, cheerful, and gentle-concern.
Pulse's "thinking" state shall be the user-visible indicator during courseware generation, replacing job-queue/pipeline dashboards.
Pulse shall walk the instructor through syllabus field completion on request (e.g., drafting an ILO from the CHED reference).
Pulse shall deliver the Fig. 2 scripted confirmation prompts ("Are you okay with the uploaded syllabus?", "What do you want to do next?") as part of its dialogue, not as a separate modal system.
Pulse shall surface grounding citations conversationally on request ("This draws on Topic 3.2…") rather than via a standalone provenance viewer.
Pulse shall never present model-selection, cost-tier, or prompt-template controls; those remain internal.
Pulse's dialogue shall be dismissible with one action and shall not block the underlying screen (non-modal by default).
Pulse shall respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and offer a static/reduced-animation mode.

Pulse's per-role vocabulary shall differ (e.g., "flag students below threshold" for instructors/Dean; "here's what to review" for students), but the character and interaction model shall be identical across roles.
Pulse shall be draggable from its docked position by mouse or touch.
Dropping Pulse onto a designated page zone (syllabus builder, courseware, curriculum, performance, review inbox) shall open a focused, conversational session scoped to that zone's task.
The focused session shall dim/blur the rest of the screen so attention stays on the dropped-on zone and the assistant panel; the zone itself shall remain sharp and highlighted.
Dropping Pulse outside a designated zone shall be rejected with a brief visual cue (not a silent no-op or an error dialog) and Pulse shall return to its docked position.

The focused session shall open by asking what the user wants to do, offering role-scoped intents specific to that zone (e.g., "Build a new syllabus" vs. "Edit an existing one") rather than a single generic prompt.
Once an intent is chosen, Pulse shall guide the user step by step, one step visible at a time, with the ability to go back, and a visible step count.
The user shall be able to exit a focused session at any point (a dedicated exit control, or clicking outside the highlighted zone), which fully restores the page to its prior state.

A guided step may link to another page when the task requires navigating there; following it shall exit the current focused session and carry the conversation forward as a normal Pulse message on arrival.

Each zone's guidance shall be authored by a dedicated task-specific agent module (`src/agents/`), not by branching logic inside the Pulse component itself — a new workflow gets a new agent, not a rewrite of Pulse.

An agent shall declare which roles it applies to and which intents are visible to each role; Pulse shall refuse a drop (per FR-GUIDE-18) if the current user's role has no matching agent for that zone.

The agents directory shall be scoped to the five real EduPulse workflows (syllabus, courseware, curriculum/import, performance, review) — not to speculative subsystems (model governance, reviewer certification, licensing, forensic tooling) absent from Ch.1-2.

Dragging shall not interfere with Pulse's existing click-to-chat behavior — a click (no meaningful pointer movement) opens the normal chat drawer; only a real drag-and-drop enters the focused zone mode.

On a drop, Pulse shall describe the actual component from the page (kind, label, current state, required/disabled, constraints and on-page help), never reading values of password, contact or payment fields.
Pulse shall offer a walkthrough generated from the visible, labelled controls of the dropped component or its section; a step on a required empty field waits for the user's input.
A rejected drop shall show a visible reason (outside the page, role not permitted, sensitive field); a successful drop perches Pulse beside the component with the panel on the opposite side.
When an authored walkthrough step's control cannot be found on the page, Pulse shall say so instead of silently highlighting nothing.

Pulse shall turn a conversation into proposed app actions (register an attached class list, add a material to the knowledge library under a course, generate a week of courseware, search records, open a page) through deterministic rules; model output never selects or runs an action.

An action that changes data shall show exactly what will change (course, block and students; course and title; outline week and the items kept) and run only after the user presses its confirm button. **Cancel** changes nothing, and a registration can be undone. Each finished action links to the page that shows its result.

An instructor's attached class list (CSV, Excel, PDF, Word or text) shall be read into students with ID, name, email and block, with the course and block detected from the file. A second list for the same course and block merges without duplicates; rows without a student name are reported, never guessed. The Syllabus → My Courses uploader shall use the same reader.

For an attached material, Pulse shall rank the courses it matches by keyword and embedding similarity against course titles, descriptions, outcomes and syllabus outline weeks, and show the matched words and where in the course each appears.

A search request shall return the matching registered students, class lists, courses, courseware and library documents the user's role may see, each naming its source and opening the page that shows it. A request to open a page shall navigate only to routes the role may open.

When a request names a course that has a syllabus in the user's workspace, Pulse shall add that syllabus as a cited reference. A material added under a course shall keep the course in its title and record, so later answers cite it by course, title and page.
Instructors shall upload PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, TXT, Markdown and CSV files up to 4 MB; content type shall be verified from the bytes and must match the extension.
Extraction shall run in an isolated worker with heap and time limits and no access to server secrets; archive bombs, encrypted files and oversized documents shall be rejected before parsing.

Extracted text shall be cleaned (repeated headers/footers, page numbers, broken lines) and scored for quality, with instruction-like text flagged; the user shall review or correct the text before it is indexed.
Indexed passages shall keep page/slide and section metadata so citations identify exact locations.
Embeddings and reranking shall use free, open models running in-process with pinned, checksum-verified files; no API key shall be required for retrieval.
Retrieval shall combine vector similarity and full-text search with reciprocal rank fusion, then rerank with a cross-encoder and keep diverse sources.

Pulse shall answer through named LangGraph agents (Guardian, Planner, Researcher, Ranker, Comparator, Writer, Verifier, Corrector, Librarian) and show each answer's agent timeline. The Guardian was added by the October 4, 2026 correction (FR-AGENT-02).
Every generated claim shall be checked against the sources; claims supported by two or more documents shall be marked corroborated; numbers, names and absolute statements must agree with the source.
Wrong or missing citations shall be corrected automatically; unsupported statements trigger at most one revision, then cited source excerpts replace an unverifiable answer.
Users shall be able to request a revision of an answer with their own note.
Instructors shall compare two library documents and see shared, related and unique points with coverage; this is never plagiarism or authorship detection.

Pulse shall suggest real references from free open catalogs (Open Library, OpenAlex, Wikipedia) through fixed endpoints with validated responses; references are suggestions requiring instructor verification.
Each generated courseware draft shall show automatic outline coverage per topic and outcome and statement verification before instructor review.
Retrieval, abstention and verification quality shall be evaluated on real, openly licensed documents with reproducible scripts.

Courseware generation shall follow the outline week's plan. Every listed topic shall be searched and checked for coverage; a topic made only of common words (such as `for` or `while`) counts only where the draft uses it as a keyword. The activity and assessment shall follow the planned activity and assessment. Each question's explanation must support its marked answer: a contradicting key is sent back for one revision, and any disagreement that remains is shown to the instructor. The References section shall list only the week's syllabus resources and teaching materials and the knowledge-library passages used; links the syllabus does not list are removed.

PDF pages without a text layer shall be readable with OCR on the user's device. Page images are never uploaded, and only pages without text are read. The text keeps its `[[Page n]]` markers. Pages below 70% confidence and pages with no text are named. The OCR text passes the same cleaning, quality and instruction checks and instructor review as any upload (FR-RAG-03).
The system shall support five account roles: system admin, Dean, Associate Dean, Instructor and Student. The system admin is not an academic role and does not replace the Dean or Associate Dean.

The system admin shall sign in with the owner's Google account; the other roles sign in with provisioned email and password. An account without an assigned role shall be refused at sign-in and by the API.

The system admin's console shall show service health checks, role coverage, account creation and role assignment (through a server-side function that verifies the admin), and an audit log of actions filterable by success and failure.
The owner's admin account shall be able to switch its view into any of the five roles while keeping its admin identity, AI key and data; no other account can switch.
Every named agent shall have a registered job title, the task it works on and a measurable goal; the answer timeline, AI settings and admin console shall use this one registry.

A Guardian agent shall check each Pulse request before any other agent works. It shall decline: (a) learners' requests to answer, solve or check assessment items; (b) plagiarism or AI-authorship detection, integrity scoring, at-risk prediction and proctoring; (c) computing official grades. A decline shall explain what Pulse can do instead and cite the rule. Rules are deterministic, and the displayed role may add learner rules but never lift them.

Each Pulse or courseware run by a signed-in account shall be recorded with its workflow, task, outcome, triggered rule, provider and model, duration, evidence and claim counts, and each agent's goal result. Records shall never contain prompt, answer or document text, and a user can record only their own runs.

The system admin's console shall show, for each named agent, its task, its goal, runs, goal-met rate, fallbacks or stops, average time and last run, plus appropriate-use declines by rule and recent runs by role (never by person).

Agent run records shall use the OpenTelemetry GenAI agent naming (`gen_ai.operation.name` = `invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.agent.name`), so an open-source tracing tool can read them later without a schema change.

The Guardian's decisions and the document injection scanner shall be evaluated with a reproducible script: labelled project cases, the openly licensed deepset/prompt-injections dataset with a held-out test split, and real course documents to count false flags.
Settings shall expose exactly one AI-provider control: a choice between a locally hosted model and a free API key, entered once.
Settings shall not expose model registries, adapters, circuit breakers, or per-model tuning parameters.
Settings shall include Account (name, email, password) and Appearance (theme, font scale) sections.
Settings shall include a Notifications section to control which events generate an in-app notification.
Settings shall include a Data & Privacy section limited to: export my data, request account data deletion.
Settings shall not include a tenant-wide feature-flag or integrations catalog.
Language selection (English/Filipino) shall live in Settings, not the top bar, once a user has set a preference.
The AI-provider control shall be visible to Dean and Instructor roles only; Students shall not see AI configuration.
Every Settings change shall take effect without a page reload.
The system shall notify instructors when a syllabus is approved or returned for changes.
The system shall notify students when new courseware is published to their section.
The system shall notify instructors when generation for a requested batch completes.
The Dean shall be notified when a syllabus or courseware item is submitted for review.
The notification bell shall show an unread count and open a scrollable list from the top bar.
The system shall not generate notifications for internal system-operations events (job retries, model latency, storage).
The system shall provide a single Help & Support destination reachable from the top bar on every screen.
Help content shall cover the five-step workflow in Fig. 2 in plain language.
Help shall include a contact path to institutional technical support.
The system shall not maintain a separate multi-tab knowledge-base/training-module authoring surface.
Static legal pages (Privacy Policy, Terms of Use) shall be reachable from the footer, outside the authenticated shell.
